articles.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
articles.summary: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well‑contested and at times breathless derby.
body: Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s strike in the second half appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story.

However, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually secured when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area. That late strike left City second in the Women’s Super League table, now behind Chelsea on goal difference, and the result breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race.

United were markedly improved on the league meetings last season with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time, however, Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test and, although they may feel they should have finished the game off earlier in the second half, few could argue that a draw was not a fair result.

articles.title: What have Man Utd changed to turn around WSL form?
articles.summary: It is a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month - and they proved it to fight back and earn a point against rivals Manchester City.
body: Derby day underlined the changing picture at Manchester United, with Eva Olid's team proving they are made of stern stuff by fighting back for a point against rivals Manchester City.
This was the strongest performance yet under new head coach Olid, who after a slow start is seeing signs of real progress, exemplified in a hard-earned 1-1 draw on Sunday.
United not only ended City's 100% start to the Women's Super League season, but they have also extended their own unbeaten streak to eight matches in all competitions.
It is a remarkable turnaround considering United were without a win and low on confidence after their opening three WSL games.

articles.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
articles.summary: Job in balance after 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. Howe is director of football Jason Wilcox’s top candidate. Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as head coach after he oversaw another torrid defeat, against Bournemouth at Old ­Trafford on…
body: Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said of his job prospects. “I’m not expecting anything in ­particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal and I love this place.”
But the United executive are actively ­considering his dismissal, the ­Guardian understands, with the expectation at the club being that Carrick will be sacked.

Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential ­targets.
Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given that Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

articles.title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point
articles.summary: Régis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra-balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.
body: His bottom-placed team had arguably just about deserved a second Premier League win of the season but, instead, had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.
While Daniel Farke will doubtless regard his resilient side’s fifth league draw of the season as a fair return on the windblown road, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.

At least Le Bris’s side ended a run of four straight league defeats on a day when they could have done without meeting James Trafford’s goalkeeping excellence. “It’s so hard to win games,” said Sunderland’s manager. “But it’s a positive point; we played with intensity and togetherness. We were Sunderland today.
It’s still a long journey but I think we’ve shown we’re embracing the challenge. We probably deserved more today. But there’s no drama, no panic.”

articles.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd owners' problems far bigger
articles.summary: Manchester United's fans sang their support for Michael Carrick during the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, but voiced their opposition to virtually everything else.
body: There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.
It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss.
But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for Carrick, with his bosses in serious talks over his future.

However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise.

articles.title: Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for world title
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.
body: Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower.

And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention.

But Antonelli has moved 123 points clear of Russell, and 124 points clear of Hamilton, with just a maximum of 125 left to play for this season to make a coronation at next Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix all-but inevitable.
Antonelli, who only turned 20 in August and is in his second season of F1, will clinch the title with four rounds to go in Mexico if he finishes anywhere in the top nine.

articles.title: Russia to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships
articles.summary: Moscow is set to host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, marking the first time a world championship for an Olympic sport will be held in Russia since the start of the Ukraine war.
body: The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) confirmed the news on Sunday, four months after it announced Russian and Belarusian athletes would be eligible to compete in IWF events.
The Federation added that Ahmedabad, India, will host the 2029 World Weightlifting Championships.
"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the Championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," IWF General Secretary Jose Quinones said.
"It is also worth noting that three of these four countries will be organising an IWF world event for the first time - Kosovo, Venezuela and India.

articles.title: City's perfect start ended in derby draw with Man Utd
articles.summary: A late equaliser from Elisabeth Terland earned Manchester United a well-earned 1-1 draw that ended Manchester City's perfect start to the WSL campaign.
body: City looked set for victory as Khadija Shaw finally broke the deadlock with a little over 20 minutes to go. However, it was Shaw who inadvertently set up Terland for the equaliser in the last minute of normal time.
Both teams came into the contest in good spirits. City had made a perfect start in their opening six WSL games, while United had been starting to click under Eva Olid.

It was the hosts who appeared more likely to find the opener following a tense first half. They were on top after the break, with Jess Park ratting the crossbar on the hour mark as they looked to make their dominance count.

Shaw had been having an uncharacteristically quiet evening, being heckled by home fans and marked out of the game by Maya Le Tissier in the first 45. She targeted Dominique Janssen when the game resumed and the switch paid off.

articles.title: Rodgers backs 16-game 'NFL International week' after Paris history
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers endorsed the introduction of an international week to the NFL season as he led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris on Sunday.
body: Rodgers and the Steelers made history last year when they beat the Minnesota Vikings in the NFL's Dublin debut at Croke Park, before travelling overseas again this week to deliver another milestone moment for the league in the French capital.
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell revealed on Friday that the league has plans to play a game in Tokyo, Japan in either 2027 or 2028, with wider ambitions of reaching 16 international games per season.

"I really look forward to that. We know that soccer worldwide probably has the most amount of fans. If you watch the World Cup at all, you know how fanatical the people for their country teams are. But the NFL is still shown in a number of countries, the Super Bowl is shown in over 100 countries; the reach of the league is fantastic," said Rodgers.
"I think I always wanted to be a part of it. I remember the 2011 CBA, there was talk about expanding the amount of international games, didn't really a whole lot until the second CBA.

articles.title: FOX Sports To Broadcast Special Veterans Day Weekend From Military Academies
articles.summary: Long before Sunday kickoffs and Saturday rivalries, West Point and Annapolis stood as the bedrock of American duty. For the United States' historic 250th birthday celebration FOX Sports will be honoring its heroes on Veterans Day weekend. Coverage kicks off Saturday, Nov. 7, at 10 a.m.
body: The pregame lineup features Rob Stone, Urban Meyer, Matt Leinart, Brady Quinn, and Mark Ingram II. The star-studded lineup also features Chris "The Bear" Fallica and Tom Rinaldi, along with special guests broadcasting live from Trophy Point on West Point’s campus.

The hype surrounding the matchup continues to build, as both programs enter the contest playing well. The Black Knights remain firmly in The American Championship mix, while the Falcons sit near the top of the Mountain West standings at 5-2.

Last year’s matchup saw a 20-17 finish that went the Black Knights' way. The Falcons’ defense has remained a force ever since, allowing just 20.9 points per game this season to set up another showing on the field between two of the sport’s most prestigious programs.
This is more than a game. It’s a true celebration of what makes America so special and a meaningful way to honor our nation’s 250th anniversary.
